title: Garry Tan on YC, building without playing business, and AI-era distribution and startups
summary: Garry Tan (YC CEO) explains why YC's simple process works, why founders must set their own frame and talk to real customers, and why creators win distribution. He argues LLMs with good evals let small teams replace rote knowledge work and build huge businesses.

principles.text: Don't let media or competitors define your game; you'll end up playing the wrong one.
principles.quote: when you're not careful, you sort of allow media or other people to sort of frame your reality and then you just play the wrong game.

principles.text: Focus on your own users and profitability, not the game investors or press push you into.
principles.quote: just play your own game. Like make up your own mind.

principles.text: Build your worldview from first-source customer data, not from narratives told to you.
principles.quote: it's important to build your worldview on how the world works directly from customers and their customer data.

principles.text: Businesses must act like creators, otherwise they pay the big ad networks for attention.
principles.quote: if you're running a business today, you kind of have to be a creator because if you're not a creator you got to buy eyeballs somehow

principles.text: AI startup play: find firms spending heavily on rote knowledge work and replace it with LLMs plus workflow and evals.
principles.quote: go and find real people who like are running businesses and they're spending hundreds of thousands of dollars a year on giant teams of people doing like rote, repeating knowledge work.

principles.text: Ideas alone aren't enough; you must act, talk to users and build.
principles.quote: you actually have to go with your hands and go talk to users and you know, sit and build a thing.
